standards.name: Sprint Goals Documented
test: Open the Sprints report under the board's Reports tab in Jira and list all sprints closed in the last quarter.
Open each closed sprint's details in Jira and flag any blank Sprint Goal or goal entered after the sprint start date.
Read the goal text of a random sample of five sprints per team in Jira and check each states a business outcome, not a task list.
Open the sprint review notes for the same sampled sprints in Confluence and find the met/partially met/not met notation.
Pass when every closed sprint has a goal set by sprint start and each sampled goal states an outcome assessed at review.

standards.name: Status Tracked Through Lifecycle
test: Open the ADR directory in the architecture repository on GitHub Enterprise and list the status header of every ADR.
Filter to Deprecated ADRs and open each in GitHub Enterprise to find the link or ID of its superseding ADR.
Open the file history in GitHub Enterprise for five ADRs that changed status in the past six months and read each change entry.
Pass when every ADR shows Proposed, Accepted, or Deprecated, each Deprecated ADR links its successor, and changes are dated.

standards.name: Stewardship Assigned
test: Export the full asset inventory from the enterprise data catalog and flag assets with a blank or Unassigned steward or domain.
Export the active-employee roster from the HR system and match every listed steward against it.
Open the assignment history in the enterprise data catalog for departed stewards and check successors within the 30-day window.
Email the listed stewards of five critical datasets (policy, claims, premium) from Outlook to confirm accountability.
Pass when zero assets lack a named steward and domain, no vacancy exceeds 30 days, and all five stewards confirm ownership.

standards.name: Strategic Alignment
test: Open the scoring model configuration in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview) and list the named strategies behind alignment scoring.
Open the current strategic plan in Confluence and compare its approved objectives to the taxonomy in the PPM tool.
Open 5 recently scored initiatives in the PPM tool and check each strategic-mapping field names at least one objective.
Run the last intake cycle's scoring report in the PPM tool and list initiatives scored above minimum without a mapped objective.
Pass when the taxonomy matches the approved plan, unmapped initiatives hold the minimum score, and no exception is found.

standards.name: Structured JSON Logging
test: Pull a recent 100-line log sample from the central log platform (Splunk) for five services spanning different domains.
Run a field-presence query in Splunk asserting timestamp, service_name, severity, and event details on each sampled service.
Run a cross-service severity=ERROR search in Splunk over all five services and note any parse errors returned.
Pass when every sampled line is valid JSON with all four mandatory fields and the cross-service query returns zero parse errors.

standards.name: Tech Debt Tagged in Backlog
test: Run a filter for the designated tech-debt tag in Jira and export all items with description and estimate fields.
Open each tagged item in Jira and flag any missing a compromise description or a remediation effort estimate.
Open the last three sprint retrospective pages in Confluence and list every mention of newly discovered debt.
Search pull request review comments in GitHub Enterprise for the same sprints and note debt mentions lacking a tagged Jira item.
Open the shared tech-debt backlog view in Jira and capture a screenshot showing the standard tag taxonomy in use.
Pass when every tagged item has description and estimate and each debt found in retros or reviews has a same-sprint Jira item.

standards.name: Technical and Business Metadata Required
test: Export 15 assets registered in the last 60 days from the enterprise data catalog with all metadata fields.
Open each sampled asset in the enterprise data catalog and check schema, data types, source system, and load mechanism.
Check each sampled asset in the enterprise data catalog for a plain-language description and at least one linked glossary term.
Register a test asset in the enterprise data catalog leaving the description blank and note the platform response.
Open the asset-quality dashboard in the enterprise data catalog and list incomplete assets with remediation owner and due date.
Pass when all 15 assets carry both layers, the test registration is blocked or flagged, and no incomplete asset exceeds 30 days.

standards.name: Test Data Management
test: Open the test data registry in Confluence and flag any integration-suite dataset not labeled synthetic or masked.
Run the dataset refresh pipeline in GitHub Actions to generate a fresh dataset on demand.
Run the integration suite twice in GitHub Actions against the fresh dataset and compare the two pass/fail result sets.
Open the dataset version manifest in the repository on GitHub Enterprise and check each version tag and schema changelog entry.
Export the last 90 days of lower-environment data provisioning requests from ServiceNow ITSM and check masking sign-offs.
Pass when no unmasked production data is referenced, both runs match, datasets are versioned, and all copies show sign-off.

standards.name: Test Pyramid Observed
test: Run the test-count report stage for the current sprint in the CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) and export counts per layer.
For any repository where e2e or UI tests outnumber unit tests, search Jira for a rebalancing item with an assigned target date.
Open the latest engineering health review page in Confluence and confirm each inverted-pyramid repository was discussed.
Open three recent pipeline runs in GitHub Actions and record runtime per layer and the count of distinct e2e journeys.
Pass when unit tests dominate, e2e is smallest with under ten scenarios, unit runs finish under two minutes, and flags have items.

standards.name: Timeliness Per Business SLA
test: Export the governed dataset list from the enterprise data catalog with each documented availability SLA and consumer sign-off.
Extract 30 days of delivery timestamps per governed dataset from the monitoring platform (Datadog) and compare to each deadline.
For each breach found, search ServiceNow ITSM for the incident ticket and check it was opened within the notification SLA.
Open the SLA performance dashboard in the monitoring platform (Datadog) and compare its breach count and on-time rate.
Pass when every dataset has a signed-off SLA and each breach in the 30-day sample has an alert, a timely ticket, and is reported.

standards.name: Two Approvers Required
test: Open Settings > Branches on each repository in GitHub Enterprise and check required approvals is two with author approval off.
Open 10 recent merged pull requests on protected branches in GitHub Enterprise and record approver identities against the author.
Check in each sampled pull request on GitHub Enterprise that one approver matches a CODEOWNERS entry for the changed paths.
Raise a test pull request with a single approval on a protected branch in GitHub Enterprise and attempt the merge.
Open the CODEOWNERS file at the repository root in GitHub Enterprise and check owners cover /src, /infra, and /config.
Pass when protection requires two non-author approvals with code-owner coverage and the single-approval merge is blocked.

standards.name: Two-Week Sprints
test: Export all active Scrum teams' sprint configurations for the current quarter from Jira and record each sprint duration.
For every team not on a 14-day sprint, open the deviation approval record in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview).
Check each approval in the PPM tool for a documented operational constraint and an expiry or review date.
Reconcile the PPM deviation register count against the count of non-standard configurations in the Jira export.
Pass when every sprint is 14 days or covered by an approved, constrained, dated deviation and the reconciliation shows zero gaps.

standards.name: UAT Sign-Off
test: Export the list of reports promoted to production in the past quarter from ServiceNow ITSM with linked UAT sign-off records.
Open each UAT sign-off record in ServiceNow ITSM and check it carries a named business-owner signature, not a proxy.
Open the signed UAT requirements checklist in Confluence and compare figures, filters, and layout to the production report.
Review the change log in ServiceNow ITSM and flag any production report release without a closed, linked UAT approval ticket.
Pass when every promoted report has a signed business-owner UAT record, matches requirements, and no release lacks approval.

standards.name: Use Event-Driven Patterns
test: Open the integration design for a state-change workflow in Confluence and check it publishes a named domain event to a broker.
Search the producer's repository in GitHub Enterprise for direct consumer endpoint calls in the state-change code path.
Open the event schema registry (Confluent) and check each event has a versioned schema and independently registered subscribers.
Pull the last consumer-outage incident report from ServiceNow ITSM and read the producer availability metrics for the window.
Pass when events publish with versioned schemas, the producer calls no consumer directly, and it stayed healthy in the outage.

standards.name: Used for Planning
test: Open the Velocity report under the board's Reports tab in Jira and record the last six completed sprints' velocities.
Compute the rolling average and compare the current sprint's committed points against it in the Jira sprint report.
For commitments over 20% above average, open the planning page in Confluence and find the product-owner sign-off and rationale.
Open the team working agreement in Confluence and check the 3-6 sprint lookback window is documented.
Pass when commitments track the rolling average and every overage above 20% carries a recorded sign-off with rationale.

standards.name: Velocity Calculated
test: Open the sprint closure reports for the three most recent completed sprints under the board's Reports tab in Jira.
List each sprint's accepted stories in Jira and check carried-over and rejected stories are excluded from the velocity figure.
Recalculate velocity for two sprints from the accepted-story points in the Jira export and compare to the recorded figure.
Open the team working agreement or Definition of Done in Confluence and check the calculation method is formally defined.
Pass when recorded velocity counts accepted points only, both recalculations match, and the method is documented and stable.

standards.name: Vulnerability Scanning of Third-Party Libraries
test: Open the pipeline definitions for three applications in GitHub Actions and check an SCA step runs on every build.
Review the last 10 build logs per application in GitHub Actions and flag any run where the SCA step was skipped or bypassed.
Download the latest SBOM artifact per application from GitHub Actions and check dependencies, versions, CVEs, and its date.
Cross-reference five dependencies per application against the NVD feed and match critical and high CVEs to Jira tickets.
Push a branch adding a dependency with a known critical CVE and watch the SCA step in GitHub Actions fail the build.
Pass when SCA runs on every build, SBOMs are current, every critical or high CVE is ticketed, and the seeded CVE blocks the build.

standards.name: Weekly Knowledge Sharing Sessions
test: Open the team calendar in Outlook for the past 8 weeks and list every scheduled knowledge-sharing session per team.
Open the session index page in Confluence and match a recording or indexed summary link to each of the 8 weeks per team.
Play 3 randomly sampled recordings from the index in Confluence and note the topic, named presenter, and technical content.
Ask 2 team members who do not maintain the legacy life and annuity systems to find a relevant recording in the Confluence index.
Pass when all 8 weeks show a held session with an indexed recording, samples cover concrete topics, and both searches succeed.
